contents.name: Proposition 1.2(c)
contents.reason: The tensor-product construction concerns contravariant forms on a different module operation. No tensor-product representation construction is needed to define, normalize, or use the form on one Verma module here.

contents.name: Proposition 1.2(d)
contents.reason: The orthogonal-complement assertion is a general submodule-form tool. The planned radical proof instead uses the unique maximal Verma submodule, so this separate complement formalism is not a prerequisite.

contents.name: 2, Simple Submodules of Verma Modules
contents.reason: This section develops the distinct question of a unique simple submodule. The selected construction needs the unique simple quotient; relating the two requires later Verma-homomorphism or duality machinery.

contents.name: Proposition 2.1
contents.reason: Its unique-simple-submodule statement is not used by the maximal-submodule quotient argument. It belongs with the later study of embeddings and duality, rather than being an omitted prerequisite here.

contents.name: 3, Homomorphisms between Verma Modules
contents.reason: This is precisely the next representation-theory pair's subject: it turns singular vectors into maps and studies their dimensions. The present page supplies the universal property it will consume, but does not pre-empt that development.

contents.name: Theorem 3.1
contents.reason: The injectivity and dimension bound for maps between Verma modules are RL-3 statements. They are not needed for the construction of a Verma module, its form, or the determinant criterion on this page.

contents.name: Theorem 4.2
contents.reason: The theorem's embedding conclusion is an instance of the Verma embedding criterion. That criterion is deliberately scheduled in RL-3 after this page has established singular vectors and determinant hyperplanes.

contents.name: Remark 3.2
contents.reason: The convention that identifies a nonzero Verma homomorphism with an embedding belongs to the next page's map-and-linkage discussion. It is not needed to form the present quotient or calculate its determinant blocks.

contents.name: Corollary 4.4
contents.reason: This identifies a simple submodule along a dot-orbit and uses the embedding story deferred to RL-3. The current page's rank-one quotient example does not require this general linkage consequence.

contents.name: 5, Block Decomposition of Category O
contents.reason: Block decomposition requires the ambient category O, finite-length, and central-character organization. Those definitions and finiteness obligations belong to the explicitly scheduled RL-4 page, not this Verma-module scaffold.

contents.name: Theorem 5.1
contents.reason: The identification of the linked subcategories as blocks is a category-O theorem. It depends on the category and its composition-factor framework, both intentionally deferred to the dedicated RL-4 page.

contents.name: 8, Highest weight modules and Verma modules
Corollary 8.10
contents.reason: The classification of irreducible highest-weight modules is broader than the quotient construction selected here. It is a consequence after the present construction, not a lemma required by the form or determinant proof.

contents.name: Proposition 8.12
contents.reason: This is the finite-dimensional classification criterion for arbitrary semisimple g. The page supplies one explicit sl2 quotient as a boundary check, but does not undertake the dominant-integral classification theorem.

contents.name: Exercise 8.14
contents.reason: These exercises construct homomorphisms and embeddings between Verma modules. They are the intended subject of RL-3 and are not assumed by the determinant proof on the current page.

contents.name: Exercise 8.13
contents.reason: This exercise introduces expectation values and contragredient Verma modules. Those dual and tensor constructions are neither required for the single-Verma Shapovalov form nor within the selected pair's stated scope.

contents.name: Definition 15.1
contents.reason: The categorical finiteness definition is expressly scheduled for RL-4. Only the formal character calculation is needed now, and it is stated with its completed-formal-series convention rather than importing Category O.

contents.name: Example 15.2
contents.reason: The example places Verma and contragredient Verma modules inside Category O. The former is already constructed here, while the Category O and restricted-dual assertions belong to the later finiteness-and-duality page.

contents.name: Lemma 15.3
contents.reason: This lemma supplies category-O finiteness behavior beyond a single Verma module. The present page proves directly that each PBW weight space is finite and leaves category-wide structure to RL-4.
